title: Decide the fate of the unfiled gateway await_tx_accepted issue draft
description:
## Outcome
The draft at `/tmp/issue-draft-gateway-await-tx-accepted.md` is either filed upstream,
rewritten, or deliberately dropped -- with the reason recorded. It is currently in neither
state and lives only in /tmp, where it will be lost.

## Why this exists
The draft describes a real liveness hole: LNv2 `ReceiveStateMachine`'s `Funding` state calls
`await_tx_accepted(outpoint.txid)` with no timeout before requesting decryption shares, so a
funding transaction that never gets a verdict pins the receive SM indefinitely. That
propagates silently through `await_receive` (whose `Funding` arm is a bare `{}`) and
`relay_direct_swap`'s `operation_exists` short-circuit, so every later attempt on the same
contract blocks and submits nothing.

## Critical constraints
The draft's own "What I have NOT established" section lists five gaps, and the central one
is still open: **the funding txid and its fate were never identified.** That determines
whether the defect is the unbounded await or something upstream of it. Filing as-is risks
repeating the #8834 episode, where evidence was offered for a theory that was later
retracted and the "supporting evidence" evaporated with it
(`/tmp/issue8834-evidence-SUPERSEDED.md` records that lesson).

Also note the observations in the draft predate the #8837 diagnosis. Some of the described
stall may be the `tpe` panic killing `sm-executor` rather than this await. Re-read the
draft against that finding before filing anything.

## Scope
Decide: file, rewrite, or drop. If not filing now, move the draft OUT of /tmp so it
survives.

## Verification
- Acceptance signal: the draft is out of /tmp, and either an upstream issue link exists or
  a written reason for dropping it does.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The draft no longer lives only in /tmp.
- [ ] Either an upstream issue link exists, or a written reason for dropping it does.
- [ ] The draft has been re-read against the #8837 finding before any filing.
close_reason: Landed via PR #5. Decision: do not file (observed stall attributed to #8837 tpe panic, not the await hole; central txid unknown never resolved). Draft moved out of /tmp into docs/superseded/ with reasoning; hardening notes retained.

title: Allocator fee bounds and refusal diagnostics
description:
## Outcome
The allocator bounds move fees proportionally instead of absolutely, and a refusal records
enough to explain itself after a restart.

## Why this exists
Two live defects, both verified in production behaviour on 2026-07-21:

1. Sizing subtracts the FULL absolute `max_fee` from the source's surplus
   (`wallet-core/src/allocator.rs:51-58`, `:84-92`), so a cap large relative to surplus
   saturates `available` to zero and refuses the move outright.
2. `min_move` is 5 sats (`tick.rs:198`) while the fee budget is 200 sats
   (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:44`), so a 40:1 fee-to-amount move passes every check today.

Separately, a real refusal was observed that could NOT be reproduced from policy + balances
(hand-computed: available = 1,937,774 msat, positive; a move for exactly that amount later
succeeded). The refusal path records only `fed` + `reason`, so there is no evidence to
diagnose it with.

## Scope
Refusal diagnostics; the proportional fee cap; the per-pair economic floor design.

## Non-goals
The wider bps rewrite (`spending_floor_bps` / `max_federation_bps` / routing-first free
path). Reviewer Concern 9 split this work out deliberately: it is independent, same-day
value with no coupling to that rewrite. Concerns 1-8 in the design doc stay OPEN and are
not owned here.

## Critical constraints
- Greenfield: no backwards compat, no migration shims, no serde compat layers.
- This is money-moving allocator code. The project record is that rb-lite never converges
  on it (24 rounds on 5.2a; 12+ then killed on 5.2b). Implement manually, dual-review with
  codex + fable, merge. Do NOT drive this with an rb-lite loop.

## Spec refs
`~/.gstack/projects/fedimint-wallets/master-main-design-20260721-031500.md`, section
"Decisions Locked (2026-07-21, post cross-model adjudication)" — decisions 1-6, each
adjudicated by two independent reviewers and re-verified locally.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] An observed refusal is fully explainable from its journal row alone, with no live logs.
- [ ] No combination of policy and balances with positive surplus refuses a funding move via
      fee-cap saturation.
- [ ] An evacuation of a small dying-federation remnant still succeeds (the proportional cap
      did not leak into the Evacuate path).
- [ ] The per-pair economic floor is either implemented, or has a written design with all five
      open questions closed and an implementation bead created.
- [ ] Reviewer Concerns 1-8 in the design doc remain untouched and explicitly out of scope.
close_reason: All four children closed (.1 diagnostics persist, .2 proportional cap + evacuate absolute cap, .4 refusal diagnosed as benign co-emission, .3 route-economics design settled). Success criteria met: refusals row-reconstructible (+br-nsx max_fee_bps), no fee-cap saturation, evacuate remnant drains, per-pair floor has a settled design + impl bead (br-route-economics-impl-hc3). Reviewer Concerns 1-8 untouched.

title: Persist refusal diagnostics by widening OperationKind::Refusal
description:
## Outcome
A `RefuseInflow` decision writes the figures that produced it into the journal, so a
refusal can be explained after a pod restart without live tracing.

## Why this exists
A real refusal on 2026-07-21 could not be reproduced from policy + balances. Hand
arithmetic at the observed balances (spending 3,936,126; standby 1,987,774; target
50,000,000; max_fee 50,000) gives available = 1,937,774 msat -- POSITIVE -- and a move for
exactly 1,937,774 later succeeded. So the refusal is unexplained, and nothing on disk
records why. Every downstream fee-policy decision is currently being designed on top of an
unreproduced failure.

## Scope
Widen `OperationKind::Refusal` (`wallet-core/src/ledger.rs:129`) to carry the decision
figures, thread them from `Action::RefuseInflow` through the mapping, and populate them at
the construction sites.

Verified site list (10 references; 6 need edits):
- `wallet-fedimint/src/journal.rs:1016`, `:1060` -- construction, must supply new fields
- `wallet-core/src/ledger.rs:286` -- the mapping, must pass them through
- `wallet-cli/src/main.rs:3690`, `wallet-core/tests/ledger.rs:467` -- test construction
- `wallet-cli/src/main.rs:2763`, `:2820` -- bind `{ fed }` with no `..`; will not compile
  until `..` is added
- `wallet-cli/src/main.rs:2934`, `wallet-daemon/src/handlers.rs:794`,
  `wallet-core/src/ledger.rs:386`, `wallet-fedimint/tests/ledger.rs:481` -- already
  `{ .. }`, untouched

Figures worth carrying (at minimum): `want`, `available`, `cap_room`, `min_move`, and the
surplus inputs that produced `available`.

## Non-goals
Does NOT add fields to `Action::RefuseInflow` as the primary mechanism. That was the
original plan and it is WRONG: `journal.rs:993` destructures `RefuseInflow { fed, .. }` and
`ledger.rs:286` maps to `OperationKind::Refusal { fed }`, so anything added to the Action
variant persists NOTHING. The Action may still carry the figures as the transport, but the
`OperationKind` widening is what makes them durable.

Does not change refusal semantics, reason codes, or when a refusal is emitted.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Follow the existing precedent for values unknown at row-creation time:
  `Receive`/`Pay`/`DirectInflow` all carry `Option<..>` fields (`ledger.rs:98-119`).
- Greenfield: no serde compat layer, no migration for old rows. There are no old rows.
- The six `refuse_decision` call sites are `allocator.rs:37, 146, 188, 192, 403, 417`; not
  all of them have the same figures available, which is why optional fields fit.

## Dependencies / ordering
None. Independently claimable, and should go FIRST -- it is the only bead that makes the
open refusal mystery legible. Does not block the proportional cap work, but its output
should inform whether that work is aimed at the right failure.

## Verification
- Unit tests: `wallet-core/tests/ledger.rs` -- assert the mapping carries the figures
  through, including the None case.
- Integration / e2e: `wallet-fedimint/tests/ledger.rs:481` already asserts a Refusal row is
  written; extend it to assert the figures survive a journal round-trip.
- Logging / observability: this IS the observability work. Confirm a refusal row read back
  from the journal is sufficient to recompute the decision by hand.
- Acceptance signal: take the next observed refusal in the pilot, read its journal row, and
  reproduce the decision arithmetic from that row alone with no live logs.

## Spec refs
Design doc "Decisions Locked" #1. The CRITICAL regression test previously added for the
Action-payload shape is REMOVED as part of this bead -- see decision #2; it guarded journal
rows that cannot exist, which is the exact failure the greenfield-no-backwards-compat
learning records.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `OperationKind::Refusal` carries the decision figures; all 6 edit sites compile, including
      the two `wallet-cli` patterns that need `..` added.
- [ ] A refusal row read back from the journal is sufficient to recompute the decision
      arithmetic by hand.
- [ ] The stale regression test guarding the Action-payload shape is REMOVED.
- [ ] `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` all pass.

## Progress (implemented, pending dual-review)

Branch `feature/refusal-diagnostics`, commit `c3b723d`. All gates pass: full workspace
`cargo test` (23 test-result groups, 0 failures, incl. 4 new tests), `cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

**Design decision (load-bearing, for the reviewers):** `RefusalDiagnostics` does NOT
participate in `Action`/`OperationKind` equality — a hand-written `PartialEq` returns true
always. This is not a convenience: `actor.rs:1958` compares two full `Action::RefuseInflow`
values with `==` in the production sizing-conflict recheck, so if the figures affected
equality, an attach carrying different incidental figures would spuriously read as a
`SizingConflict`. Excluding them makes equality agree with the idempotency key (`idem_refuse`
already excludes them). Consequence: the 11 refusal goldens stayed green with only a
one-line macro change, and diagnostic CONTENT is asserted by dedicated tests instead of
mirror-goldens.

**Real blast radius was ~17 sites across 8 files, not the estimated 6.** Enumerated by the
compiler: `Action::RefuseInflow` gained a field (all pattern/construction sites), plus
`OperationKind::Refusal`. Fixed: allocator (6 refuse_decision calls), ledger mapping,
journal (2 construction sites), tick.rs (3 `matches!` patterns), wallet-cli (3 patterns + 1
test construction), and test constructions in wallet-core/tests/{ledger,executor} and
wallet-fedimint/tests/{ledger,move_plan}.

**Decision #2 (drop the stale regression test) was vacuous:** the "CRITICAL regression test"
was only ever a PLANNED item in the design doc — it was never committed to code (confirmed:
no serde/round-trip test of a refusal payload existed). So "removed" = "not added".

**Acceptance signal met in test form** (`record_refusals_persist_diagnostics_across_serialization`):
figures survive the serde_json round-trip that backs restart durability. The LIVE acceptance
(read a real pilot refusal's row and reproduce its arithmetic) is br-ljj.4's job.

REMAINING GATE before merge: dual-review with codex + fable (epic constraint — money-adjacent
allocator code, rb-lite is banned here). Not yet done.

## Dual-review DONE (codex gpt-5.4 xhigh + fable), findings addressed — commit `67dfc32`

Both reviewers: NO P0/P1, sound and mergeable. Fable ran the full suite and actively tried to
break the always-true `PartialEq` — could not; confirmed sound (no Hash/Ord contract violation,
independently verified here too). Both independently confirmed my justification #2 (actor
sizing-conflict recheck) was DEAD — refusals are filtered as non-executable before any attach
(actor.rs:582, executor.rs:625) — so the equality design now rests only on agreeing with the
idempotency key. Reworded, not reverted (fable's call: sound, keep it).

Findings incorporated (all verified against source before acting):
- P2 (both): row was not self-decomposing. Added `source`, `source_spendable`, `max_fee` — the
  cap-too-large case now shows max_fee explicitly instead of an opaque `available=0`.
- P2 (codex): evacuation zero-amount refusal comment was FACTUALLY WRONG (`safest_other`
  guarantees positive dest cap room, so amount==0 means source drained). Fixed comment + record
  honest figures.
- P3 (fable): over-cap key collision (target>cap misconfig) dropped figures. `push_decision` now
  prefers the populated refusal; guarded to refusal-vs-refusal (safe — no reservations, no
  move-key collision).
- P3s: standalone `show` now prints figures; doc fixes; 3 new tests (receive-blocker, no-source,
  collision).

Gates re-run green: full `cargo test` (0 failures), `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D
warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean. Two commits on `feature/refusal-diagnostics`
(c3b723d + 67dfc32), ready to open a PR / merge.

## Live-visibility fix — commit `f48d6a5`

Followed up the P2-a review finding (figures unreadable on a running walletd): added an
optional `refusal` object to the `OperationView` wire DTO, populated it in the daemon
mapping, and rendered it in both client and standalone `show` via one shared helper. The
"frozen DTO" precedent was overridden by explicit user instruction; the DTO already carried
an `error` diagnostic field, so this is consistent. A wire round-trip test asserts every
figure survives serialization field-by-field (equality alone can't, given always-equal
`PartialEq`) and that the field is omitted for non-refusals. Three commits total on
`feature/refusal-diagnostics` (c3b723d + 67dfc32 + f48d6a5); gates green.

## Second dual-review (codex gpt-5.6-sol + fable) on the FULL 3-commit diff — commit `64e727d`

Re-ran under the stronger `gpt-5.6-sol` (the skill's current default; earlier round used 5.4),
this time covering the walletd DTO commit (f48d6a5) which had never been reviewed.

- **fable: APPROVE, no blocking findings.** Ran the full suite + clippy + fmt; verified the
  always-eq PartialEq, push_decision replace, evacuation figures, and the DTO round-trip all
  sound. Confirmed the actor-recheck-unreachable claim TRUE.
- **codex-sol: 1 P1 + 2 P2.** The P1 (old refusal rows fail to decode post-deploy) was
  VERIFIED but OVERSTATED — `scan_ledger_rows` skips + warns (not catastrophic); refusals carry
  no budget. USER DECISION: stay greenfield-pure, no `#[serde(default)]` shim (old figure-less
  refusals skip on read; only explicit `show <old-key>` errors).

Fixed (verified): CLI duplicate `amount_msat` → `decision_amount_msat`; figure-less refusals
omit the wire `refusal` object (were 8 nulls); evac records `max_fee: None`; `available`
decomposition docs scoped honestly.

DEFERRED (fable P2, with rationale): plain-over-cap and no-destination-evacuation refusals
record no dest-side figures. fable itself called it "documented scope, not a bug"; those are
secondary classes, the over-cap condition is checkable live (balance vs policy cap), and the
motivating fund-refusal case is fully covered — declined to grow the struct further (reviewer
ratchet). Candidate follow-up if over-cap diagnosability becomes a need.

Four commits on `feature/refusal-diagnostics` (c3b723d, 67dfc32, f48d6a5, 64e727d); gates green.

title: Proportional move fee cap (max_fee_bps_of_move) with absolute cap retained for Evacuate
description:
## Outcome
Allocator-emitted `Move`s are bounded by a fee cap PROPORTIONAL to the amount moved, so
sizing scales instead of saturating to zero, and a fee can no longer be a large multiple of
the amount it moves. `Evacuate` keeps its absolute cap.

## Why this exists
Two verified defects:

1. **Saturation.** `allocator.rs:51-58` (top-up) and `:84-92` (standby) compute
   `available = spendable - outbound - debited - max_fee`, reserving the FULL absolute cap
   up front. A cap large relative to surplus drives `available` to 0 and the move is
   refused outright. Evacuation is already exempt from this reservation
   (`allocator.rs:388-395`).
2. **No economic relation between amount and fee.** `min_move` is 5 sats (`tick.rs:198`)
   and the default fee budget is 200 sats (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:44`), so a 40:1
   fee-to-amount move passes every check TODAY. The proportional cap is what closes this --
   it is not a new risk introduced by this change.

## Scope
- Add `max_fee_bps_of_move` to `Policy` (`wallet-api/src/lib.rs:8-33`, note
  `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`) and thread it into `TickPolicy` / `AllocatorSnapshot`.
- Change funding-move sizing to `amount + fee_cap(amount) <= budget`, i.e.
  `amount <= surplus * 10_000 / (10_000 + bps)`.
- Stamp the proportional cap on `Action::Move`'s `fee_cap` (`allocator.rs:443`).
- Choose and DOCUMENT a provisional default bps value.

## Non-goals
- `min_economic_move` as a scalar policy constant is DROPPED. The economic floor is
  per-pair and belongs to the design bead, not here.
- Does NOT touch the wider bps rewrite (`spending_floor_bps`, `max_federation_bps`,
  routing-first). Design doc Reviewer Concern 9 split this out on purpose.
- Does not change `per_fed_cap`, which has a second consumer at `executor.rs:1108`.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **`Evacuate` MUST keep the absolute `max_fee`** it carries today
  (`Action::Evacuate { fee_cap: snapshot.max_fee }`, `allocator.rs:410`). A proportional cap
  on a small dying-fed remnant computes below any realistic gateway base fee -- 1 sat on a
  100-sat remnant at 100bps -- so the evacuation refuses and the remnant is LOST with the
  federation. "Replace max_fee with bps everywhere" is the natural-looking change and it is
  WRONG. Both knobs stay in `Policy`; they bound different risks. Confirmed by two
  independent reviewers.
- The default bps value is a genuine open item. The design doc declines to guess
  ("Unknown until observed", Open Question 4). Pick one informed by gateway fees actually
  observed in the pilot, and record the rationale in the commit -- do not silently invent a
  round number. A too-tight cap refuses viable moves; a too-loose one permits expensive
  ones.
- Perform-time enforcement already exists and is pre-commit: receive-side at
  `executor.rs:1116-1135`, total at `Pay` (`executor.rs:1261`, `:1780`). This bead changes
  what cap is HANDED to that machinery, not the machinery.

## Dependencies / ordering
Independent of the refusal-diagnostics bead; both are ready immediately. BLOCKS the
route-economics design bead, because the per-pair economic floor is defined against `bps`.

## Verification
- Unit tests: sizing algebra -- assert `available` never saturates to zero for any
  (surplus, bps) pair with positive surplus; assert an `Evacuate` of a balance at or below
  the absolute cap is still emitted.
- Integration / e2e: **56 golden tests in `wallet-core/tests/allocator_golden.rs`** will
  move. Expect the diff to be mostly golden churn and review it as such -- a golden that
  changes in an unexpected DIRECTION is the signal worth chasing.
- Also touches `wallet-cli` clap flags and `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md` (the procedure
  the pilot depends on). Total blast radius estimated at ~125 references across 16 files;
  treat as a multi-session change, not a 45-minute one.
- Acceptance signal: reproduce the original saturation case -- a cap exceeding surplus --
  and show a move is now emitted and correctly sized.

## Spec refs
Design doc "Decisions Locked" #3; Reviewer Concern 9 (split-out rationale) and Concern 7
(blast radius).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `max_fee_bps_of_move` exists in `Policy` and reaches `AllocatorSnapshot`.
- [ ] Funding-move sizing uses `amount + fee_cap(amount) <= budget`; no positive surplus can
      saturate `available` to zero.
- [ ] `Evacuate` still carries the ABSOLUTE `max_fee`, and an evacuation of a balance at or
      below that cap is still emitted.
- [ ] The chosen default bps value is documented with the rationale and the observed gateway
      fees it was derived from -- not a round number picked blind.
- [ ] The 56 goldens in `allocator_golden.rs` are reviewed for DIRECTION of change, not merely
      regenerated.
- [ ] `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` all pass.
- [ ] README.md updated -- `max_fee_bps_of_move` adds a user-facing CLI flag, and the repo
      convention requires README updates for any user-facing change (not as an afterthought).
close_reason: Landed via PR #3 (squash 157bd87). Proportional funding-move fee cap with Evacuate absolute-cap carve-out; serde-default for old-row decode. Cleared two local dual-reviews, the GitHub bots, and a full multi-reviewer-loop (CLEAN). Follow-ups filed: br-m9m (seed recovery), br-nsx (bps in refusal rows).

title: DESIGN: settle route-economics open questions before implementing the per-pair floor
description:
## Outcome
A written decision for each of the five unsettled questions below, sufficient for a fresh
agent to implement `route_economics_by_pair` without inventing architecture. Ends with an
implementation bead created; this bead does NOT write the feature.

## Why this exists
The SHAPE of the economic floor is settled and adjudicated (see "Decided already"). The
FAILURE and OWNERSHIP paths are not. A plan-to-beads readiness check on 2026-07-21 refused
to encode the implementation because five questions would have had to be guessed. Guessing
them in code is how the two paths silently drift.

## Decided already (do NOT relitigate)
- The floor is `route_economics_by_pair[(from, to)]`, ORDERED-pair keyed, IO-supplied into
  the snapshot, keeping `decide()` pure. It carries `resolved_gateway`,
  `min_viable_amount`, and a status `Routable | Unroutable | UneconomicAtAnySize`.
- A SCALAR floor is wrong: `decide()` picks the pair (`fund_into`, `allocator.rs:42-72` and
  `:74-106`), the pair fixes the usable-gateway intersection (a Move's gateway must serve
  BOTH ends, `executor.rs:283-299`), and fees are quoted per-federation
  (`multi_client.rs:572-627`). Ordered, because `resolve_gateway` scans the DESTINATION's
  list (`executor.rs:268`), so each direction can pin a different gateway.
- NO closed form. The receive side is not affine in the net amount (the gateway fee applies
  to the INVOICE, hence `gross_up`'s fixed point) and the federation fee is a step function
  (`fee.rs:10-17`). Linearizing UNDER-estimates the floor -- the unsafe direction, since a
  too-low floor leaves exactly the churn the floor exists to suppress. Any approximation
  must be an explicit UPPER bound. Over-blocking self-heals (a deferred top-up's shortfall
  grows until it clears the floor); under-blocking churns forever.
- Route economics are computed FRESH every tick (~4 quotes per pair, 2 pairs). Caching was
  rejected: stale-low is the unsafe direction. Fee surfaces are NOT cached today --
  `ProbeResult` carries only `gateway_available: bool` (`probe.rs:66-71`) and `tick.rs:188-200`
  puts no fee data in the snapshot.
- O(N^2) is a non-issue: `min_move` is read only at `allocator.rs:161` and `:172`, both in
  `fund_into`, whose only pairs are (standby -> spending) and (spending -> standby). V1's
  active set is ~2 feds per ADR-0006 (`docs/phase2-plan.md:31`).
- Planning preselects the route and `perform()` honors it, rather than both paths
  re-deriving selection and being required to agree forever.

## The five questions this bead must answer
1. **Where does the preselected gateway live?** `Action::Move` has NO gateway field
   (`types.rs:120-126`) -- unlike `Action::Pay`, which does (`types.rs:141-148`). Carrying
   it means extending a serde-derived type that flows into intents and the journal. Decide:
   extend `Action::Move`, put it on the Intent, or elsewhere. Note `OperationKind::Move`
   ALREADY has `gateway: Option<GatewayUrl>` (`ledger.rs:120-127`).
2. **What happens when the preselected gateway is dead at perform time?** `perform()` can
   run much later than planning (retries, restarts). Re-resolving reintroduces the exact
   mismatch this design removes; failing terminally strands the move. This is the central
   failure path and it is undecided.
3. **How is `min_viable_amount` searched?** Over what range, with what termination, and
   under what RPC budget? Each probe is an async quote and the fed fee is amount-dependent.
   Unbounded quoting inside a tick is a real hazard.
4. **How does this interact with `pinned_gateway`?** `resolve_gateway` short-circuits on a
   pin (`executor.rs:265-267`). Preselection's relationship to that is unstated.
5. **What is the fallback when an entry is missing or `Unroutable`?** One reviewer proposed
   falling back to the protocol floor alone (permissive, transient, with the perform-time
   cap still protecting money); the other proposed relying on the status variants. No
   decision was recorded.

## Non-goals
Does not implement `route_economics_by_pair`. Does not touch the wider bps rewrite.

## Critical constraints
- `UneconomicAtAnySize` (bps set below the gateways' combined ppm) must be VISIBLE -- it
  silently disables rebalancing for that pair forever, which is a misconfiguration. Unlike
  the sub-dust skip, which stays deliberately silent (`allocator.rs:156-163`).
- Adjacent finding worth landing regardless: the Move path takes the FIRST validating
  gateway with no fee comparison (`executor.rs:260-282`), while the raw-receive arm scans
  candidates tracking `lowest_quote` (`executor.rs:963-975`). Today a Move pays whatever
  the first serving gateway charges. Decide whether to fix that here or split it out.

## Dependencies / ordering

title: Diagnose the unexplained 2026-07-21 refusal using the new journal figures
description:
## Outcome
A written root cause for the refusal that motivated this entire epic, or a positive
statement that it can no longer occur and why.

## Why this exists
This is the failure that started the work, and it is STILL UNEXPLAINED. Hand arithmetic at
the observed balances says a move should have been emitted:

    spending 3,936,126   standby 1,987,774   target 50,000,000   max_fee 50,000
    want      = 46,063,874
    available = 1,987,774 - 0 - 0 - 50,000 = 1,937,774   (POSITIVE, not saturated)
    cap_room  = 96,063,874
    amount    = min(want, cap_room, available) = 1,937,774

and a move for exactly 1,937,774 msat later succeeded. `min_move` is 5,000 msat, nowhere
near binding. So neither the fee-cap saturation bug NOR the dust floor explains it.

Candidates never ruled out: a stale or differently-timed snapshot than the balances
recorded; `usable_source` returning None because the standby fed carried an
`evacuation_reason` (`allocator.rs:250-253`); or a destination-side block. Note the gateway
was panicking on #8837 (`tpe::aggregate_dk_shares`) during this window, which is the
leading hypothesis and would ALSO explain why the move succeeded later, after the tpe
backport landed.

## Why this is a separate bead
The instrumentation bead (br-ljj.1) makes the evidence exist. It does not commit anyone to
reading it. Without this bead the epic can close with the original defect still open --
which is exactly how this failure survived once already.

## Scope
Read the journal figures from the next refusal (or a replayed one), reconstruct the
decision, and name the cause.

## Non-goals
Does not fix whatever is found -- that is a follow-up bead. Does not re-open the fee-cap or
floor decisions.

## Critical constraints
Do NOT accept a plausible-sounding explanation without the arithmetic reproducing. This
investigation has already produced five confident wrong diagnoses that were each falsified
on inspection (see the design doc's cross-model section). Reproduce the numbers or say it
is still open.

## Dependencies / ordering
Depends on br-ljj.1 (the figures must be persisted first). Should complete before br-yq8
reverts the debug log level, since that is the fallback evidence channel.

## Verification
- Acceptance signal: the refusal's decision arithmetic is reproduced from recorded data,
  and the divergence from the hand calculation above is named.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The decision is recomputed from persisted figures, not from memory or live logs.
- [ ] The cause is named, or the bead is explicitly left open with what evidence is still
      missing.
- [ ] If the cause is #8837, that is stated with the gateway log evidence, and the epic's
      premise is revisited.

## Note from br-ljj.1 review: figures are NOT visible on a LIVE walletd

The dual-review (P2-a) surfaced an operational limitation that bites THIS bead: the daemon's
`OperationView` DTO drops `diagnostics` (handlers.rs:794), and that DTO is treated as frozen
(project precedent rejected mutating it). So a running walletd's `history`/`show` — including
`--json` — never emit the refusal figures. They are durable in the journal, but readable only
via the standalone CLI (`show` prints them now; `--json` carries them), which needs the
exclusive RocksDB lock — i.e. walletd STOPPED.

Consequence for diagnosing the pilot refusal: either stop walletd and read via standalone CLI,
or read the row from the DB directly. Budget for that when this bead runs.

## UPDATE: live-visibility limitation RESOLVED (br-ljj.1 commit `f48d6a5`)

The note above (figures only via stopped-wallet CLI) no longer holds. `OperationView` now
carries the `refusal` figures over the wire, so a running walletd's `history`/`show`
surface them directly. Diagnosing a pilot refusal no longer requires stopping the pod.

## DIAGNOSED (commit 52a85db, branch diagnose/20260721-refusal): benign co-emission, NOT a bug

The refusal was never anomalous. `fund_into` emits a move AND a shortfall refusal in the SAME
tick (allocator.rs:207 move when amount>0; :228+ refusal when amount < want.min(cap_room)). At
the recorded balances (spending 3_936_126, standby 1_987_774, target 50_000_000, max_fee
50_000, per_fed_cap 1_500_000_000):
  want      = 50_000_000 - 3_936_126 = 46_063_874
  available = 1_987_774 - 50_000     = 1_937_774
  cap_room  = 1_500_000_000 - 3_936_126 ~= 1.496e9  (does not bind)
  amount    = min(want, cap_room, available) = 1_937_774  (> 0 -> a MOVE is emitted)
  amount (1_937_774) < want (46_063_874) -> a SpendingBelowTarget refusal is ALSO emitted
So one tick emitted BOTH a partial top-up move of 1_937_774 (the move that "later succeeded"
on async settlement) AND the refusal for the ~44M shortfall the standby couldn't cover.

**Dispositive evidence:** 1_937_774 = standby 1_987_774 - max_fee 50_000. That exact value only
arises as the co-emitted move amount, which is why the observed move matched it precisely. A
replay test at the exact balances (`diagnose_20260721_refusal_is_a_partial_topup_co_emission`,
allocator_golden.rs) asserts both the move (2->1, 1_937_774) and the refusal figures and passes.

**Root cause of the "mystery":** my own misreading. The earlier investigation looked for a
refusal INSTEAD OF a move and couldn't reconcile them; they are the same tick's two outputs.
The pre-diagnostics refusal row recorded only fed+reason, so nothing indicated a move
accompanied it. The new figures (amount>0 => a move WAS emitted; want >> amount => source
exhausted) make co-emission self-evident — which vindicates br-ljj.1: the diagnostics earn
their keep even though the motivating incident was benign.

**Acceptance vs reality:** "recompute from persisted figures" cannot be met literally for the
ORIGINAL row (it predates the instrumentation, no figures). Recomputed instead from the
recorded balances via replay; the exact amount match is equivalent evidence. NOT #8837 (that
is a gateway/executor stall, unrelated to a pure allocator decision).

**Optional residual (not required to close):** confirm on the pilot journal that the refusal
row and the move (seq=613) shared one occurrence. The amount match already implies this
(sequential ticks would not reproduce standby-minus-max_fee exactly), so it is corroboration,
not a gap.

**Epic impact:** br-ljj (refusal diagnostics) stands — the diagnostics are what made this
legible. br-ljj.2 (fee-cap saturation) remains a SEPARATE real bug, independent of this
benign incident. Closing this bead.

title: Fail-fast (503) on fresh dest-side requests to joined-but-unopened federations
description:
## Outcome
A FRESH `/v1/receive`, `/v1/direct-inflow`, or move whose destination is joined but not
currently open returns an explicit unavailable (503) at admission, instead of being admitted,
parking Pending, and (for receive/direct-inflow) stalling ~30s before a 504.

## Why this exists
Surfaced by a review bot on PR #1 and analyzed by two independent models (codex gpt-5.6-sol +
fable) plus local verification. The bot's framing was mostly WRONG and is NOT a defect (see
Non-goals), but both models independently identified one genuine, minor residue worth a
follow-up: the current path is a UX/liveness wart, not a bug.

Today: `sample_balances` (wallet-daemon/src/handlers.rs:651) omits an unopened fed, admission
treats its balance as zero and journals the op; the driver then fails closed (Retryable ->
Pending) and the watch scheduler retries `open_all` every cycle, so it self-heals when the fed
opens. For receive/direct-inflow the caller waits on `block_for_invoice` up to ~30s and gets a
504 (handlers.rs:599/638) rather than an instant 503. A fed that NEVER opens leaves an immortal
Pending row holding reservations (executor.rs:83/103/139/166) — liveness/capacity pressure, not
stranded money.

## Scope
An admission-time openness check for FRESH destination-side requests only, returning 503.

## Non-goals / must-preserve (critical — both models flagged this)
- NOT a blanket precheck in the handlers. Existing Pending/Awaiting/completed idempotent
  requests MUST remain attachable, and an already-created invoice MUST remain retrievable even
  if the destination is temporarily closed (durable journal state, actor.rs:1621/1632). A naive
  unconditional check breaks attach + idempotent replay.
- Does NOT reverse the park-and-retry design. Project history records that a general
  "unopened-fed pre-check" was reviewed and REJECTED in phase-6a step-5 as forbidden
  new-handling with no money-loss. This bead is narrower: fail-fast for FRESH requests only,
  preserving attach/retrieval — not an admission refusal for all cases.
- No money-safety change: nothing is debited before the destination opens (verified: receive/
  inflow debit no source; in a move CreateInvoice precedes Pay and needs dest-side calls that
  fail Retryable while closed, executor.rs:1175 before :1309).

## Critical constraints
Distinguish FRESH from EXISTING intent at admission (nonce/key lookup) before returning 503.
Consider also terminalizing or GC-ing immortal Pending rows for feds that never open (separate
concern; may be its own bead).

## Dependencies / ordering
Independent. Pre-existing behavior (sample_balances, since commit 4aaef17); not blocked by
anything.

## Verification
- Unit/integration: a FRESH receive/direct-inflow/move to a joined-but-unopened dest returns
  503 (not admitted, not a 30s-504); an EXISTING Pending/Awaiting intent for the same key still
  attaches; an already-minted invoice is still retrievable while the dest is briefly closed.
- Regression: the existing `tests.rs:275` behavior (joined-but-unopened -> admitted -> 504) is
  intentionally CHANGED for the fresh case; update it and assert the attach/retrieval paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fresh dest-side request to an unopened fed returns 503 with an actionable message.
- [ ] Existing-intent attach and invoice retrieval are preserved (tested).
- [ ] The park-and-retry / self-heal path for already-admitted intents is untouched.
- [ ] `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR #8 (squash). FRESH dest-side receive/direct-inflow/move to a joined-but-unopened fed returns 503 via ServiceError::DestinationUnavailable; gate rides the actor's FRESH branch after the existing-key attach (race-free, single-owner), so attach + invoice retrieval preserved; source/scheduler/probe/pay/join/standalone ungated. nix-develop fmt/clippy/test green.

title: Wire seed-based wallet recovery (ClientPreview::recover)
description:
## Outcome
The wallet can recover a federation's ecash from the seed alone — a `recover` path (a `wallet-cli
recover <invite>` verb or `join --recover`) that runs fedimint module recovery, so funds are
restorable after loss of the operation/registry store, a disk move, or a fresh host.

## Why this exists
CRITICAL GAP found during br-ljj.2 review (fable P1, verified): the wallet has NO seed-recovery
path. `ClientPreview::recover` is NEVER called anywhere in the codebase — `join_inner` only ever
calls `preview.join(...)` (multi_client.rs), which `InitMode::Fresh`-initializes an EMPTY client.
So there is no way to rebuild a funded client from the seed. Consequences:
- The runbook's "wipe journal.db and rejoin recovers the ecash" was FALSE (removed): rejoin
  allocates a fresh empty db-prefix (next_db_prefix = max+1) because the registry (in journal.db)
  is gone, and `open_all` only reopens registry rows — so the funded partition is orphaned and
  `balance` reads 0.
- "Disk dies" incident recovery ("run fedimint recovery with the seed") is not actually
  implementable today.

## Scope
- A recovery-join: `preview.recover(client_db(new_prefix), root_secret, backup: Option)` instead
  of `.join(...)`; register the fed in the journal (put_federation).
- WAIT for module recovery to complete before reporting success/balance — recovery is async
  ("each recovering client module will not be available for use" during it); watch
  RecoveryProgress (fedimint-client builder.rs ~767, 805, 886) to completion, with progress
  surfaced to the CLI.
- A CLI verb (`recover <invite>` or `join --recover`) + daemon path if applicable.
- Handle the orphaned-partition case: recovering an already-partitioned fed should reuse or
  supersede the stale partition, not stack a third.

## Non-goals
Not seed-at-rest encryption (Phase 7). Not automatic recovery on startup.

## Critical constraints
Money-adjacent + async recovery = money code. Implement carefully, dual-review, do NOT rb-lite a
under-specified version (spec the wait/progress/partition-reuse interactions first). Recovery
while a send was in flight can double-pay (fedimint-mechanics §4) — the recovery verb must be a
deliberate, documented last-resort, never automatic.

## Verification
- Devimint: fund a fed, drop the journal (or use a fresh client db), `recover <invite>`, assert
  the balance is restored after recovery completes.
- Unit: the recover path registers the fed and reuses/supersedes an existing partition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ClientPreview::recover` is wired behind a deliberate CLI verb.
- [ ] Recovery waits for module-recovery completion before reporting balance.
- [ ] Live devimint gate: seed-only balance restoration passes.
- [ ] The runbook's "Disk dies" / upgrade recovery steps point at the real verb.
notes: rb-lite attempt FAILED (2026-07-23): exit 12 max_rounds — 25 rounds / ~19h / 51 iters / 4861 insertions across 30 files (multi_client +2643; also edited README/runbook/spec/scheduler), STILL 2 open P1 recovery-correctness findings at round 25 (wait-for-SMs-before-checkpoint; skip-pending-recovery-partitions-at-startup). NON-CONVERGED, unmergeable, discarded. Lesson: recovery is too large/interconnected for one rb-lite run even with a complete spec (spec completeness necessary but not sufficient — see rb-lite size caveat). Salvage patch: /tmp/rb-m9m-run/full-diff.patch (+ scratchpad br-m9m-rblite-salvage.patch) — mine its solutions (raw-read orphan scan, init-state gating, SM-readiness wait) not adopt wholesale. NEXT: decompose into small convergeable beads OR hand-build with the live devimint two-fed recovery gate. Spec remains valid at docs/wallet-recovery-spec.md.
close_reason: Implementation landed via PR #11 (69a53a2). No-wipe V1 per docs/wallet-recovery-spec.md + ADR-0025: Action::Recover, walletd restore-mnemonic, MultiClient::recover (refuse-if-registered, fresh prefix, reopen+drain+register atomically). Verified: 2 rb-lite convergences + 2 adversarial rounds (codex+fable) — an auto-double-pay found, fixed, re-confirmed CLOSED. Depends on SDK pin PR #10 (complete-or-fail recovery). LIVE devimint gate deferred to blocker bead br-recovery-live-devimint-gate-j5p (must pass before real-funds deploy). Follow-ups: br-recovery-commit-retry-syv, br-dual-open-one-race-315.

title: Implement route_economics_by_pair (per-pair economic move floor)
description:
## Outcome
Implement `route_economics_by_pair`: a per-federation-ordered-pair economic move floor,
IO-supplied into the `AllocatorSnapshot` so `decide()` stays pure, that suppresses the
uneconomic-churn the flat/proportional caps cannot. Design is fully settled in
`docs/route-economics-decisions.md` (br-ljj.3) — implement it without reopening the design.

## Scope (per the five settled decisions + the adjacent finding)
1. Snapshot field `route_economics_by_pair[(from,to)] -> { resolved_gateway, min_viable_amount,
   status: Routable | Unroutable | UneconomicAtAnySize }`, populated by IO in `tick.rs`
   (today the snapshot is fee-thin: only `max_fee`, `max_fee_bps_of_move`, `min_move`).
2. Gateway selection: replace the Move path's FIRST-validating-gateway pick
   (executor.rs ~260-282) with the CHEAPEST gateway serving BOTH ends, computed from the same
   fee quotes the floor needs (argmin combined fed+gateway fee). `resolved_gateway` is that pick.
3. `min_viable_amount`: a fixed ~4-quote affine UPPER-bound model (round every fee component up)
   + a hard per-tick quote cap. No unbounded in-tick search. Over-blocking is the safe direction.
4. `gateway: Option<GatewayUrl>` (`#[serde(default)]`) on `Action::Move` and `Action::Evacuate`,
   stamped by `decide()` from `resolved_gateway`. `assemble_record` (executor.rs ~199-232) uses
   it as the cached gateway; the field enters the persisted Intent format (hence serde default).
5. Perform-time fallback (Q2): use `action.gateway` iff it still validates (serves both ends);
   else re-resolve (cheapest serving both ends) under the UNCHANGED proportional `fee_cap` — the
   cap, not gateway identity, is the money backstop. Record the actual gateway in
   `OperationKind::Move.gateway`.
6. `pinned_gateway` precedence (Q4): the pin overrides route economics entirely; compute the
   pair against the pin; `UneconomicAtAnySize` under a pin is still surfaced.
7. Fallbacks (Q5): missing entry -> permissive protocol floor (`min_move`); `Routable` ->
   `min_viable_amount`; `Unroutable` -> skip the pair's funding; `UneconomicAtAnySize` -> skip
   AND surface VISIBLY (a persistent diagnostic / refusal reason — it silently disables
   rebalancing for the pair forever otherwise).

## Non-goals
Does not change the proportional-cap knob. Does not add caching of route economics (stale-low is
the unsafe direction — computed fresh every tick, ~4 quotes/pair × 2 pairs).

## Critical constraints
`UneconomicAtAnySize` MUST be visible (unlike the deliberately-silent sub-dust skip). Any floor
approximation MUST be an explicit UPPER bound (under-estimating churns forever; over-blocking
self-heals). Money-adjacent allocator code: implement carefully with dual-review.

## Verification
- Golden tests: each status branch (Routable/Unroutable/UneconomicAtAnySize + missing-entry
  permissive fallback); the upper-bound floor's monotonicity; the cheapest-both-ends selection;
  the perform-time hint-with-cap fallback.
- Live devimint: a pair whose bps is below the combined ppm defers (UneconomicAtAnySize,
  surfaced); a viable pair moves; the move takes the cheaper of two serving gateways.
- `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` (run inside `nix develop`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `route_economics_by_pair` in the snapshot, IO-populated, `decide()` still pure.
- [ ] Move gateway selection is cheapest-serving-both-ends, not first-validating.
- [ ] `min_viable_amount` is an explicit upper bound with a bounded per-tick quote cost.
- [ ] `Action::Move`/`Evacuate` carry the preselected gateway (`#[serde(default)]`).
- [ ] Perform-time fallback re-resolves under the unchanged `fee_cap`; pin precedence honored.
- [ ] `UneconomicAtAnySize` is surfaced; missing-entry falls back permissively.
- [ ] Golden + live-devimint gates pass.

## Refs
`docs/route-economics-decisions.md` (br-ljj.3, the settled design). Depends on the proportional
cap (br-ljj.2, landed).
close_reason: Merged in PR #14: route_economics_by_pair per-pair economic floor. Validated by workspace suite (706 tests) + live devimint move + responsiveness gates; adversarial-reviewed (2 rounds, all findings resolved).

title: complete_recovery commit lacks autocommit retry
description: fable re-review of br-m9m: FedimintJournal::complete_recovery (journal.rs:576/616) uses begin_transaction + commit_tx_result with NO autocommit retry, unlike set_status_if. A concurrent watch-cycle write to the same candidate key can conflict-fail an hours-long recovery replay's commit. Outcome is SAFE (partition never registered, intent Failed, retry recovers into a fresh prefix) but wasteful — a whole replay discarded on a commit conflict. Add autocommit-retry to the complete_recovery commit. Not a money-safety defect; efficiency/robustness only.

title: Dual open_one race on an ordinary registered fed
description: fable re-review of br-m9m (pre-existing on origin/main, NOT introduced by recovery): two concurrent open_one calls for the same ordinary registered fed — the scheduler's open_all racing a user join's open (multi_client.rs ~204; open_all does not take join_lock) — can briefly run two ClientHandles on one partition before one Arc is dropped. Narrowed by recovery's new has_client early-return but not eliminated for the non-recovery path. Serialize open_one on join_lock (or a per-fed open guard) so a registered fed is never double-opened. Low severity (brief, self-healing), but two handles on one partition is the forbidden state.
notes: PROMOTED P3->P2 (codex analysis): two handles on one partition is a product-forbidden invariant (multi_client.rs:543). Close before the final soak. Pre-existing (scheduler open_all races a user join's open; neither takes join_lock).
close_reason: Merged in PR #15: serialize open_one under join_lock (public entry + open_one_locked body for join_inner), plus a commit-time drop-if-present guard. codex adversarial pass: no regression. Deterministic race is covered by the release soak this unblocks.

title: Live devimint recovery gate — pre-deploy blocker for seed recovery
description:
## Outcome
The seed-recovery feature (br-m9m, landed) passes a live devimint recovery gate. **This MUST
pass before the pilot receives real funds** — it is the spec's mandatory acceptance
(`docs/wallet-recovery-spec.md` "Verification"), and it has never run.

## Why this exists
br-m9m recovery is verified in code (2 rb-lite convergences + 2 adversarial review rounds; an
auto-double-pay found, fixed, and re-confirmed closed), but has ZERO live validation. Recovery
is money-critical (rebuilds ecash from the seed), so a live end-to-end pass is required before
any real-funds deployment. Merged (PR #11) on code-verification strength with this gate as the
deploy blocker.

## The gate
Build devimint + the wallet binaries (see docs/devimint-runbook.md: `nix develop -c cargo build
--workspace --bins`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR=~/p/fedimint/target-nix`, `add_target_dir_to_path`;
1 fed suffices — `devimint --num-feds 1 dev-fed`). Then:
1. Join a fed, receive ecash (lnv2 — mind the await-send-before-await-receive ordering, release
   bins, gateway pw; see [[devimint-lnv2-reliable-validation]]).
2. Record the balance, seed, and invite.
3. Simulate total store loss: a FRESH data dir (empty client.db + empty journal.db), same seed —
   this is the UNregistered path recovery supports (D3 refuse-if-registered).
4. `walletd restore-mnemonic < seed.txt`, then `wallet-cli recover <invite>`, then `await-move`.
5. Assert the balance is restored after recovery completes.

## Traps (from memory)
Rebuild wallet-cli/walletd with the explicit CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR before every smoke (stale
binary trap, [[devimint-dev-fed-is-single-fed]]). devimint is a built binary, not on PATH by
default.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live 1-fed devimint: fund -> fresh store -> restore-mnemonic + recover -> balance restored.
- [ ] The recovered fed is spendable (UserApproved, allocator-eligible) — send from it post-recovery.

Independently verified on a fresh devimint --num-feds 1 run: restored EXACTLY 491646 msat, RECOVER_GATE_EXIT=0. Produced via supervised rb-lite (watched closely: no assertion-weakening, main.rs change comment-only, live pass confirmed independently). Recovery is now cleared for real-funds deploy.

title: Bound the preview under join_lock; recovery terminal-visibility window
description:
## Outcome
Two money-safe concurrency/visibility refinements on the recovery path, surfaced by the
multi-reviewer-loop over the merged br-m9m PR (#11). Neither is a money-safety defect.

## 1. Unbounded preview under join_lock (join family)
MultiClient::recover (multi_client.rs:305-316) holds join_lock across an UNBOUNDED
ClientBuilder::preview — an unreachable/slow fed makes recover hold join_lock indefinitely,
queueing all future joins/recoveries (NOT money ops — pay/receive/move don't take join_lock).
This is PRE-EXISTING: user-initiated join() (join_inner with deadline=None) has the same pattern;
only the scheduler's join_before_deadline bounds the preview. The comment at multi_client.rs:302-304
falsely says "bounded preview fetch". Fix: bound the preview fetch under a deadline for the join
FAMILY (join + recover), and correct the comment. Re-verify recover's reservation invariants hold
when preview times out (Drop drops the reservation; fresh partition never allocated → safe).

## 2. Recovery terminal-visibility window
Between complete_recovery's commit and the in-memory clients.insert (multi_client.rs:379-382), a
status GET observes the intent as succeeded while /v1/balance can still read 0 for the fed. Narrow
(microsecond window), money-safe, self-correcting on the next poll. Fix: gate terminal status/balance
reads on active_recoveries so the op reads in-progress until the client is installed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Preview fetch under join_lock is bounded for join + recover; comment corrected.
- [ ] A status/balance read during the commit->insert window does not report succeeded+zero-balance.
- [ ] cargo fmt/clippy/test green (nix develop); recovery reservation invariants re-verified.
close_reason: Merged in PR #16: bounded the preview under join_lock (recover + join, 60s cap) and closed the recovery commit->insert visibility window (is_recovering-gated status). Gate green (706 tests); codex adversarial pass clean; reservation invariants re-verified.

title: Fix fedimint pin: carry the #8838 single-share TPE fix
description:
## Outcome
The fedimint pin the wallet builds against contains the #8838 single-share TPE fix, so lnv2
decryption on a SINGLE-GUARDIAN federation does not panic. Verified via a single-guardian
regression gate.

## Why — VERIFIED hard blocker (codex analysis, confirmed against the git objects)
The current pin douglaz/fedimint@5bd145c (and its base 63ab515) do NOT contain #8838
(`e350cd7 fix(tpe): correct lagrange multiplier for a single share`). At crypto/tpe/src/lib.rs:210
`lagrange_multipliers` filters to `j != i`, gets an EMPTY iterator for a single decryption share
(a single-guardian fed), and `.reduce(|a,b| a*b).expect("We have at least one share")` PANICS —
the #8837 bug that killed the client sm-executor and froze cross-fed ops. devimint runs 4 guardians
(threshold 3) so NONE of the smokes exercise this; single-guardian PILOT feds hit it on every lnv2
decryption. Pre-existing (63ab515 lacked it too), but a hard blocker for a single-guardian real-sats
build. The deployment carries a separate local tpe backport; the REPO pin does not, so any rebuild
regresses.

## Scope
- Cherry-pick e350cd7 (#8838) onto the fork stack (currently 63ab515 iroh + recovery-fix). Push the
  new immutable commit to douglaz/fedimint; bump wallet-fedimint/wallet-cli/wallet-daemon Cargo.toml
  pins (all revs) to it; refresh Cargo.lock; nix-develop build+test green.
- Add a single-guardian TPE regression gate (the case devimint's 4-guardian setup cannot catch): a
  unit test in crypto/tpe (or a wallet-side test) asserting aggregate_dk_shares over ONE share does
  not panic and yields the correct key; OR a 1-guardian devimint receive smoke.
- Re-run the cross-fed move + recovery devimint smokes against the repointed build.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The pin's tpe lib contains the #8838 fix (single-share lagrange returns 1, no panic).
- [ ] Single-guardian regression gate passes; would fail on the pre-fix pin.
- [ ] cross-fed move + recovery smokes green on the repointed build.
close_reason: Landed. Pin bumped to douglaz/fedimint wallet-pin/iroh-recovery-tpe8838 (72b1e5b) carrying #8838 (e350cd7). Single-guardian TPE regression gate (test_roundtrip_single_guardian) green; would panic on the pre-fix pin. Wallet build+test green; recovery devimint smoke green on the repointed build (both phases restored EXACTLY 491646 msat). The single-guardian panic (#8837 sm-executor freeze) that devimint's 4-guardian setup cannot catch is now closed.

title: wallet-web: crate skeleton, config, init, fail-closed startup
description:
Create the `wallet-web` binary crate: config, `init`, fail-closed startup.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.0, §6c.1, §6c.6. Posture: ADR-0028.
The spec is authoritative and complete — follow it rather than improvising.

Required:
1. New workspace member `wallet-web` (binary). A CLIENT of walletd over HTTP with a bearer token,
   exactly like wallet-cli. NEVER opens client.db or journal.db (daemon holds exclusive locks).
2. Bind address is HARD-CODED to 127.0.0.1 — only the port is configurable (default 9737). Do not
   add a bind-address config option: it would let 0.0.0.0 satisfy this spec while breaking the
   fixed exposure posture.
3. The daemon URL must be http:// and resolve to LITERAL LOOPBACK; fail startup otherwise, or a
   typo ships the full-access bearer token in plaintext to a remote host.
4. `wallet-web.toml`, written 0600 with the mode RE-ASSERTED after write (mirror
   wallet-daemon/src/config.rs). Holds: port, daemon URL, token path, Argon2id PHC hash, session
   idle/absolute timeouts, and `public_origin` (explicit scheme+host+port, NOT derived from Host).
5. `wallet-web init`: no-echo prompt, confirm, enforce a 12-char minimum, reject >1024-byte input
   BEFORE hashing, hash with Argon2id at pinned params (m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1), write config.
6. Server REFUSES TO START with no hash, a malformed PHC string, or params below those minimums.
   Fail closed: no default credential, no "auth disabled until configured", no setup page.

Tests: init writes 0600; startup fails with no hash / malformed PHC / weak params; startup rejects
a non-loopback daemon URL (there is NO bind-address test -- the address is a hard-coded
constant, not configuration); passwords under 12 chars rejected;
oversized input rejected before hashing.

Scope guard: no routes, no auth logic, no templates here. Do NOT touch the daemon. No JS toolchain.
Greenfield: no backwards-compat or migration code.
7. Structured `tracing` logging is initialised at startup (level configurable). NEVER log the
   password, the session token, the daemon bearer token, or a full invoice -- at any level.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] wallet-web builds as a workspace member and starts, serving nothing yet.
- [ ] The bind address is a hard-coded loopback constant: no config key can change it (the config struct has no bind-address field at all).
- [ ] Startup EXITS NON-ZERO with a clear message when any of these hold: no password hash configured; malformed PHC string; Argon2id params below the pinned minimums (m=19456, t=2, p=1); daemon URL not http:// literal loopback.
- [ ] wallet-web init writes the config 0600, verified after a run under umask 000.
- [ ] init rejects a password under 12 chars, and rejects >1024-byte input BEFORE hashing.
- [ ] Every criterion above is covered by a test that runs under the default cargo test.
- [ ] Startup initialises structured tracing at the configured level.
- [ ] A grep of the tree finds no log statement carrying the password, session token, bearer token,
      or a full invoice, and a test asserts the auth path logs none of them on success or failure.

title: wallet-web: Argon2id login, sessions, CSRF, security headers
description:
`wallet-web` authentication: Argon2id login, sessions, CSRF, security headers.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.2 (authoritative — implement exactly). ADR-0028.
This is the ONLY control protecting full CLI parity including /v1/recover. Treat it as such.

Required (each of these was a review finding; none is optional):
1. Every route requires a session EXCEPT `GET /login`, `POST /login`, `GET /healthz`. There is NO
   static-asset exemption — inline the login page's CSS/JS into that page.
2. Cookie: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, HOST-ONLY (no Domain). `Secure` is set iff the
   configured `public_origin` scheme is https — NEVER from the request and never from
   X-Forwarded-Proto. The sidecar terminates no TLS, so a request-derived condition can never fire
   and the cookie behind an HTTPS proxy would be permanently non-Secure and stealable.
3. Session record is `token -> {created_at, last_seen, csrf_secret}`. The CSRF secret is a SEPARATE
   256-bit CSPRNG value; the session cookie must never be echoed into HTML.
4. Regenerate BOTH values on every successful login regardless of any presented cookie (fixation).
5. Sliding 4h idle + absolute 24h, enforced server-side every request. Polling and /healthz are
   PASSIVE: they validate but must NOT update last_seen, or 3s polling keeps a tab authorized for
   the full 24h and the idle timeout never fires.
6. A loopback peer address does NOT authenticate. X-Forwarded-For is not trusted for anything.
7. Rate limiting: global, checked and incremented ATOMICALLY BEFORE any hashing so concurrent
   attempts cannot slip past the 5-failure boundary. Argon2 on a bounded blocking pool; no lock
   held across hashing or backoff, so logins cannot starve authenticated requests.
8. CSRF: session's csrf_secret in a hidden field on every mutating request, constant-time compared.
   `POST /login` is exempt from the token (no session yet) but NOT from the origin check. Origin
   (or Referer fallback) must match `public_origin` EXACTLY (scheme + host + effective port). A
   Referer is a FULL URL (`https://host/form`), so PARSE AND NORMALIZE it to its origin triple
   before comparing -- never string-compare the whole value, which rejects every legitimate
   request. Reject a Referer carrying credentials, and reject malformed values. A request with
   neither header is rejected.
9. Logout is POST with CSRF and clears the server-side entry.
10. Security headers on EVERY response including login, redirects, errors and /healthz. The CSP
    MUST carry a fresh per-response CSPRNG nonce on `script-src` and `style-src`
    (`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>';
    frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'`) and the login page's inlined <style>/<script> must
    carry it. A bare `default-src 'self'` does NOT authorize inline elements and would silently
    block the login assets item 1 requires to be inlined.
11. Session timeouts are the security contract and configuration may only ever TIGHTEN them:
    values above the 4h idle / 24h absolute ceilings, or unparseable values, FAIL STARTUP rather
    than silently widening the only mitigation ADR-0028 relies on.

Tests: see spec §6c.7 items 2,3,5,6,7,8. Note item 5 specifically requires proving that continuous
3s polling still expires at 4h.

Scope guard: no step-up (ADR-0028 decided against — do not reintroduce), no multi-user, no roles.
Never log the password, session token, or bearer token. The exhaustive route-manifest test belongs
to the final bead (br-4yz), not here — most routes do not exist yet.
12. A DEDICATED ORIGIN is required. Mount at the root and set a HOST-ONLY cookie (no Domain
    attribute). Co-hosting the wallet under a path on an origin shared with another application is
    UNSUPPORTED and must be documented as such in the crate docs: no cookie attribute, SameSite
    setting, or Origin check isolates two apps on one origin -- the neighbour can fetch
    authenticated pages, read the CSRF field out of the HTML, and submit actions.
13. `Cache-Control: no-store` on every authenticated response, so balances never land in a shared
    cache or come back via the back button after logout.
14. Log failed logins and rate-limiter engagement at `warn`, carrying NO password material. The
    password is the only control in front of /v1/recover, so a brute-force attempt must leave a
    trace an operator can see -- a limiter that silently absorbs an attack is invisible.


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] THE BASELINE: the correct password authenticates and establishes a working session, and a
      wrong password does not, failing indistinguishably. Every other criterion here assumes
      login works; this is the one that proves it.
- [ ] Every route except GET /login, POST /login and GET /healthz returns 401/redirect without a session, asserted by enumerating the route table rather than a hand-listed sample.
- [ ] An unauthenticated request from 127.0.0.1 is still rejected: loopback is not authentication.
- [ ] A session expires after 4h idle AND after 24h absolute even under continuous use, and continuous 3s polling does NOT extend it.
- [ ] Session and CSRF values are both regenerated on login, and the hidden CSRF field never equals the cookie value.
- [ ] A mutating request is rejected when the CSRF token is absent or wrong, when Origin mismatches public_origin, and when both Origin and Referer are absent. A full-URL Referer on the correct origin is ACCEPTED, proving it is parsed to an origin triple rather than string-compared.
- [ ] Login rate limiting engages after 5 consecutive failures, resets on success, holds under concurrent attempts, and does not starve authenticated requests while throttling.
- [ ] A configured session timeout above the 4h idle / 24h absolute ceiling fails startup instead of widening it.
- [ ] The CSP carries a fresh per-response nonce, the login page's inline style/script carry it, and the required security headers appear on every response class including redirects, errors and /healthz.
- [ ] An authenticated session can change the password, and doing so invalidates every other session.
- [ ] The session cookie is host-only (no Domain attribute) and the app mounts at the root.
- [ ] Crate docs state that path co-hosting on a shared origin is unsupported, and why.
- [ ] Every authenticated response carries Cache-Control: no-store; a back-button navigation after
      logout does not reveal a cached balance page.
- [ ] A failed login emits a warn-level event; the limiter engaging emits one; neither carries the
      password, the session token, or the bearer token.

title: daemon: ?status=open filter on /v1/history (the one 6c daemon change)
description:
Daemon: add a `?status=open` filter to GET /v1/history.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4. The ONLY daemon change Phase 6c is permitted; ships
as its own PR against a daemon that is in production holding real funds.

Problem: LN payments can hold for hours or days (ADR-0024), but HistoryQuery accepts only `limit`
and `before_seq`, so "what is outstanding right now" is unanswerable and a days-old held payment is
effectively invisible.

Required:
1. `HistoryQuery` gains an optional `status`; `?status=open` returns exactly `Started`+`Awaiting`.
2. **Apply the filter INSIDE the journal scan, before `take(limit)`.** `journal.rs::history()`
   already filters `before_seq` inside the same iterator chain — put the status filter there.
   Filtering in the handler AFTER `history(limit, ..)` returns would filter an already-truncated
   page, so an open row behind `limit` newer terminal rows disappears — the exact failure this
   feature exists to prevent. This matches the CLI's documented "filters apply before limit".
3. Read-only: must not touch the actor, executor, or any money path.
4. Omitting `status` must be byte-identical to today's response; cursor paging must still work.
5. An unrecognised status value returns **422 `refused`** (the daemon's existing malformed-query
   contract), not 400 and never a silent unfiltered listing.
6. `history()` currently SKIPS UNDECODABLE ledger rows silently. On the status=open path that lets
   a corrupt open operation vanish while the UI says "nothing outstanding". Signal that rows were
   skipped so the caller can fail closed.

Tests: exact Started+Awaiting set; omitting status unchanged; **an open row older than MORE THAN
ONE FULL PAGE of terminal rows is still returned** (a handler-side filter must FAIL this test —
verify it does by trying that implementation); cursor paging with the filter on; unknown status →
422; skipped-row signalling.

Scope guard: no other endpoint, no SSE, no actor/executor/journal-schema/money-path changes. The
diff should be readable in one sitting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ?status=open returns exactly the Started+Awaiting set and excludes Succeeded/Failed.
- [ ] Omitting status produces a byte-identical response to today's behaviour.
- [ ] An open row older than MORE THAN ONE FULL PAGE of terminal rows is still returned. A handler-side filter applied after history(limit,..) MUST fail this test: try that implementation first and confirm it goes red, otherwise the test proves nothing.
- [ ] Cursor paging via before_seq/next_before_seq still works with the filter applied.
- [ ] An unrecognised status value returns 422 refused, never 400 and never a silent unfiltered listing.
- [ ] Skipped undecodable ledger rows are signalled in the response so the caller can fail closed rather than render an empty list.
- [ ] The pre-existing daemon suite still passes and the diff touches no actor, executor, or money path.
