description:
`wallet-web` read surface: dashboard, Outstanding, activity, operation detail, federations.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4, §6c.5. Depends on auth + the ?status=open filter.

Required:
1. Server-rendered HTML via `askama` (compile-time templates, no runtime loading, no bundler).
2. Pages: Dashboard (unified balance, per-federation breakdown, Outstanding, recent activity);
   Activity (paginated history via the existing before_seq/next_before_seq cursor); Operation
   detail; Federations list.
3. **Outstanding must follow `next_before_seq` TO EXHAUSTION**, bounded by a page cap. **If the cap
   is reached the list MUST be labelled incomplete in the UI** -- presenting a truncated list as the
   complete Outstanding set hides exactly the old held payment this feature exists to surface. Test
   the cap-hit state explicitly. One request
   returns at most `limit` rows, so rendering a single page and calling it "all outstanding" is a
   lie — the whole point is that an old held operation stays visible.
4. If the daemon signals that undecodable rows were skipped, render a **fail-closed warning**, not
   an empty/short list.
5. **Operation detail renders ONLY what `OperationView` carries** (kind, status, amount, fees,
   actor, reason, error, refusal). It does NOT show a Stranded move's preimage or leg op-ids: the
   wire DTO carries neither and the rich move record is `--standalone` only. A stranded operation
   renders its `error` string verbatim and links the runbook's stop-the-daemon recovery procedure.
   (The earlier version of this bead required the preimage; that was unbuildable inside the
   one-daemon-change budget. Do not re-add it.)
6. The browser holds NO wallet state; every page reconstructs from the daemon. No CDN, no external
   fonts, no telemetry; assets compiled into the binary.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes): never "risk engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb,
"curated", or "anonymous". Amounts in sats with msat precision where non-zero. Agent/evacuation
actions money-centric, past-tense, with reasons.

Tests: pages rejected without a session; Outstanding lists exactly the non-terminal set AND pages to
exhaustion when there are more open operations than one page; history paging follows the cursor;
skipped-row warning renders.

Scope guard: read-only — no money forms, no admin forms, no JS yet. No framework, no htmx, no npm.
Never compute or re-derive a balance or fee in the frontend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dashboard, Activity, Operation detail and Federations render with a valid session and are rejected without one.
- [ ] Outstanding lists exactly the non-terminal set, and when there are MORE open operations than one page it follows next_before_seq to exhaustion rather than showing only the newest page.
- [ ] When the page cap is reached the list is labelled incomplete in the UI, with a test for that state. A truncated list presented as complete hides the old held payment this feature exists to surface.
- [ ] When the daemon signals skipped undecodable rows, a fail-closed warning renders instead of a short or empty list.
- [ ] Operation detail renders only fields OperationView actually carries. A Stranded move renders its error string verbatim and links the runbook recovery procedure; it does NOT claim to show a preimage or leg op-ids, which the wire DTO does not carry.
- [ ] History paging follows the existing cursor contract.
- [ ] No balance or fee is computed or re-derived in the frontend; every figure comes from the API.
- [ ] No asset is fetched from a third party at runtime.

title: wallet-web: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz
description:
`wallet-web`: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4, §6c.6. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. ~50 lines of VANILLA JS compiled into the binary, doing two jobs only: polling on-screen
   operations, and disabling a submit button after click. No framework, no htmx, no bundler, no npm,
   no CDN. (Note: the button disable is a convenience — the real double-submit defence is
   render-time idempotency keys + PRG in br-t8f, because the UI must work without JS.)
2. Polling: GET /v1/operations/{key} every 3s for VISIBLE operations, stopping on terminal status
   and on `visibilitychange`. Polling is a live-view convenience, NOT the tracking mechanism —
   Outstanding is. Browsers throttle background timers and suspend mobile pages.
3. **Polling requests must be PASSIVE with respect to the session**: they must not slide
   `last_seen`, or an open tab stays authorized for the full 24h and the idle timeout never fires.
   (Enforced in br-nfz; do not defeat it here by routing polling through an activity-updating path.)
4. UI degrades honestly without JS: forms work, pages just do not live-update.
5. Daemon unreachable: READ PAGES render a clear banner. (The money/admin form-disable behaviour is
   specified in the plan but is NOT verified here: those forms are built by br-t8f and br-ucq, which
   this task does not depend on, so asserting them here would be impossible in the declared order.
   That integration check belongs to the final gate, br-4yz.)
6. `GET /healthz` is an explicit, deliberate exception to "every route requires a session" — a
   supervisor cannot log in. Restrict it to exactly two booleans (sidecar alive, daemon reachable).
   It MUST expose no balance, no operation, no federation, and no version detail, and it must be in
   the route-manifest allowlist so the carve-out is asserted rather than accidental.

Tests: polling stops at terminal status; continuous polling does not extend a session (covered in
br-nfz item 5 — do not regress it); degraded banner appears on read pages; /healthz
distinguishes sidecar-down from daemon-down and leaks nothing else.

Scope guard: no SSE, no WebSockets, no service worker, no notifications (ADR-0028 deferred all).
No second JS file, no build step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Polling updates a visible operation and stops on terminal status and on visibilitychange.
- [ ] Polling does NOT extend the session idle timer (the assertion lives in br-nfz; this bead must not defeat it by routing polling through an activity-updating path).
- [ ] Read pages render a clear banner when the daemon is unreachable. The money/admin form-disable check belongs to br-4yz, where those forms exist.
- [ ] /healthz distinguishes sidecar-alive from daemon-reachable and exposes NOTHING else: no balance, no operation, no federation, no version.
- [ ] The UI still functions with JavaScript disabled: forms submit, pages simply do not live-update.
- [ ] Total JavaScript stays under roughly 50 lines, with no framework, bundler, or npm dependency.

title: wallet-web: money surface (send, receive+QR, move, direct-inflow)
description:
`wallet-web` money surface: send, receive with server-side QR, move, direct-inflow.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5 (including "Idempotency and double-submit" and
"Money form contracts"). Depends on the read surface.

MONEY-CRITICAL. `ReceiveRequest.nonce` and `MoveRequest.occurrence` are CLIENT-SUPPLIED idempotency
inputs: a refresh or resubmit that regenerates them is admitted by the daemon as a SECOND money
operation. A JS button-disable is not a defence — the spec requires the UI to work without JS.

Required:
1. Every money form GENERATES ITS IDEMPOTENCY VALUE AT RENDER TIME into a hidden field, so a
   resubmit of the same rendered form carries the same key and dedupes at the daemon. Preserve it
   through preview/confirm/retry.
2. Pay and Move use Post/Redirect/Get so a refresh re-issues a GET. Receive and DirectInflow do
   NOT redirect -- their invoice exists only in the POST response body and a browser does not
   render a redirect's body, so they render the result in place. That is safe because the
   idempotency key is fixed at render time and the daemon re-yields the same invoice. Do NOT store
   transient result state in the sidecar to work around this.
2b. Snapshot policy-derived fields into the form. The idempotency value alone does NOT guarantee
   replay: when federation or fee cap are unset the daemon resolves them from CURRENT policy per
   POST, and for a move the resolved fee cap is an INPUT TO THE OPERATION KEY
   (handlers.rs: `let fee_cap = request.fee_cap.unwrap_or(policy.max_fee)` feeding `move_key`).
   A policy edit between the first POST and a retry then yields a different key from the same
   occurrence and admits a SECOND move. Each rendered form must submit EXPLICIT federation and
   fee-cap values.
3. Send: paste a BOLT11 invoice, show a decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) BEFORE
   submit, allow a fee cap, confirm, POST /v1/pay.
4. Receive and DirectInflow return their payable invoice ONLY in the POST response. Redirecting
   straight to the operation page would discard it — render a RESULT PAGE carrying the invoice, its
   server-rendered QR, the operation key, and a link to the detail page. Re-attaching the same
   receive key re-yields the same invoice, which also fixes refresh-loses-the-invoice.
5. QR rendered SERVER-SIDE as inline SVG (`qrcode` crate). No JS QR library, no external service.
6. Move (/v1/move) and DirectInflow (/v1/direct-inflow) forms.
7. Per-form contract: which federation (selector where the DTO accepts one, defaulted to the policy
   spending pin), which fields are optional, and units. **Amounts are exact decimal sats with at
   most three fractional digits, converted to integer msat WITHOUT floating point.** Never parse an
   amount into f64.
8. Operations here are `Actor::User` — no Actor enum change.
9. Pay is async and may settle hours later (ADR-0024). The UI must never imply settlement because
   the POST returned 2xx.

Tests: malformed invoice rejected before submit; decoded preview matches the invoice; QR payload
equals the invoice string; **submitting the same rendered receive/move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT
DISABLED produces exactly ONE operation -- and the Move case MUST edit `max_fee` between the two
submissions and still yield ONE operation**, since a test that does not touch policy passes even
when the form omits the cap and lets the daemon re-derive it into a different `move_key` (which is
the whole defect); likewise assert Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and cap across a policy
edit; the same receive key re-yields the same invoice; result page carries invoice+QR.

Scope guard: no LNURL, no Lightning Address, no on-chain, no amountless invoices. No retry, fallback
or route logic in the frontend — the engine owns that. Never re-sum fees client-side.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A malformed invoice is rejected before submission, and the decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) matches the invoice.
- [ ] Receive renders a server-side SVG QR whose payload equals the invoice string exactly.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered receive form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation and the same invoice.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation EVEN WHEN max_fee IS EDITED BETWEEN THE TWO SUBMISSIONS. A test that does not change policy between submissions passes against the broken implementation too and therefore proves nothing.
- [ ] Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and fee cap across a policy edit.
- [ ] Pay and Move redirect after POST; Receive and DirectInflow render their result in place, because the invoice exists only in the POST body. No transient result state is stored in the sidecar.
- [ ] Amounts are parsed as exact decimal sats to integer msat with no floating point anywhere in the path.
- [ ] The UI never implies a payment settled merely because the POST returned 2xx.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon.

title: wallet-web: federation, admin, policy, diagnostics surfaces
description:
`wallet-web` federation, admin, policy, and diagnostics surfaces.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. Federations: join (/v1/join), candidates (/v1/candidates), approve (/v1/approve).
2. Admin: reconcile (/v1/reconcile), recover (/v1/recover).
3. **Diagnostics panel** surfacing /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health (scheduler alive,
   watch state, daemon health). These are part of the "full parity" claim and previously had no
   page and no bead — that was a coverage gap.
4. Policy view + edit. **Read-modify-write, never reconstruct**: `PUT /v1/policy` takes a WHOLE
   `Policy`, and new policy fields ship `#[serde(default)]`, so a form that rebuilds `Policy` from
   only the fields it knows would SILENTLY RESET any field added later — including money caps. GET
   the current policy, merge the edited fields into that value, PUT the result.
5. Policy edits state units explicitly (msat vs bps). The runbook's cap arithmetic was previously
   wrong precisely because units were ambiguous.
6. Every destructive/irreversible action — recover, approve, join, policy edits — requires an
   explicit CONFIRMATION STEP on a separate page naming in plain language what will happen.
   `recover` re-seeds a wallet; `approve` decides which federations become fundable (the trust
   decision ADR-0017's probe gate protects). This is a UI affordance, NOT an auth gate: ADR-0028
   chose no step-up and this must not smuggle one back in.
7. The seed/mnemonic is NEVER exposed by any route to any session. Seed export stays CLI-only and
   daemon-stopped (runbook Day 0).

Tests: each destructive action requires passing its confirmation page; **a policy round-trip
preserves a field the form does not know about** (prove read-modify-write, not reconstruct); no
route returns seed material; diagnostics render.

Scope guard: no multi-user, no roles, no new daemon endpoints. No policy validation logic in the
frontend — submit and render what the daemon says.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.
This matters most on the confirmation pages, which must name the real consequence in plain language
rather than reassuring the user.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Join, approve, candidates, reconcile, recover and policy view/edit are reachable and function against the daemon.
- [ ] Every destructive or irreversible action (recover, approve, join, policy edit) requires passing an explicit confirmation page that names the consequence in plain language.
- [ ] A policy edit preserves a field the form does not know about, proving read-modify-write rather than reconstruct. Rebuilding Policy from known fields would silently reset serde-default fields including money caps.
- [ ] Policy units are stated explicitly (msat vs bps) on every editable field.
- [ ] The diagnostics panel surfaces /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health.
- [ ] No route returns seed or mnemonic material under any circumstance.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon, and each confirmation
      page names the actual consequence rather than reassuring.

title: wallet-web: live devimint gate + final route manifest test
description:
`wallet-web` live devimint gate + the final route manifest test.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.7. Depends on all other 6c beads.

Two deliverables:

**A. The final route manifest test** (belongs here, after all routes exist — not in the auth bead,
where most routes did not yet exist):
- Enumerate EVERY route. Each must either require a session or appear on the explicit allowlist
  (`GET /login`, `POST /login`, `GET /healthz`). A newly added route fails by default.
- Assert the required security headers on EVERY response class: authenticated pages, redirects,
  errors, the login page, and /healthz.

**B. The live gate**, driven like the existing CLI devimint gates (wallet-cli/tests/smoke_*.sh),
against a two-fed devimint with walletd + wallet-web running:
1. Log in over HTTP with the configured password.
2. Receive: create an invoice through the UI, pay it externally, see settlement appear.
3. Send: pay an invoice and see the operation terminalize.
4. Long-running tracking: an in-flight operation appears under Outstanding, then RESTART THE
   BROWSER SESSION (new client, no cookies or state) and confirm it is still listed with correct
   status — proving the UI holds no client state and the journal is the truth.
5. Kill walletd: degraded banner appears AND the money and admin forms are disabled with an
   explanation rather than failing on submit. This cross-surface check lives here, not in br-pfc:
   the forms are built by br-t8f and br-ucq, so this is the first point where every piece exists.
   Restart walletd and confirm recovery.

Run everything inside `nix develop /home/master/p/fedimint -c ...` — bare cargo fails on missing
cmake. Use release binaries and REBUILD them before the run; a stale binary silently invalidates the
gate (this has bitten this project twice).

Capture the REAL exit code into the log (write REAL_GATE_EXIT=$? and grep it) — the trailing
command's exit status is not the gate's.

Scope guard: this bead writes AND RUNS the gate. A gate that is only reviewed and never executed is
worthless, and a false PASS is worse than no gate. Before declaring green, make one assertion fail
deliberately and confirm the gate goes red.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The final route manifest test enumerates EVERY route; each either requires a session or appears on the explicit allowlist (GET /login, POST /login, GET /healthz). A newly added route fails this test by default.
- [ ] Required security headers are asserted on every response class: authenticated pages, redirects, errors, login, and /healthz.
- [ ] Live on devimint: log in, create an invoice through the UI, have it paid externally, and observe settlement.
- [ ] Live: pay an invoice and watch the operation terminalize.
- [ ] Live: an in-flight operation appears under Outstanding, SURVIVES A BROWSER RESTART with no cookies or client state, and is still listed with correct status.
- [ ] Live: killing walletd produces the degraded banner AND disables money and admin forms with an explanation rather than failing on submit; restarting recovers.
- [ ] The gate is RUN, not merely written: before declaring green, break one assertion deliberately and confirm the gate goes red.
- [ ] The real exit code is captured in the log (REAL_GATE_EXIT) rather than inferred from a trailing command.
- [ ] A repository-wide assertion proves NO route returns seed or mnemonic material: enumerate every
      route, exercise it with a valid session, and assert no response body contains the mnemonic.
      This is a global invariant, so it is asserted once here rather than per-surface.
